solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Henry's feeding green parrot

indicators.note: Henry is feeding the green word, so his letter goes inside it

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for environmentally green
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry gives his pet parrot some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Henry is feeding (going into) the green word.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words back mechanically, just as a reflected sound does.

clue.text: The English going to my home city

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
in means at home

indicators.note: the English letter is going, so it is taken away from the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone proudly says the English are visiting their home city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not a possessive but the exclamation COR.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth is an ancient Greek city, home to the church Paul wrote letters to.

clue.text: Getting pulled over won't hurt

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the word won't is hurt, knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reassurance that being stopped by the police won't do any harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like part of 'pulled over' but gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle being towed behind another is being hauled along by it.

clue.text: 21's success at cards

definitions.note: 21 is the answer to 21 Across, to faint and drop; the 's is 'is'

parts.note: a hit is a success, like a hit record
the deck is the pack of cards

explanation.surface: A cross-reference claims some answer amounts to winning at a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the solution of 21 Across, to fall down in a faint.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw oneself flat on the floor is like collapsing to the ground in a swoon.

clue.text: Learn of saying in these parts

indicators.note: saying it out loud gives a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: to learn of something is to hear about it

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a local proverb from this neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saying' looks like a noun, a proverb, but signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means somewhere near this place, locally, in this neighbourhood.

clue.text: Low in numbers tonight, under strength at end — no worries

indicators.note: worries is used as a verb: the letters are worried, tugged into a new arrangement
only the end letter of strength is used

explanation.surface: A team short of players, weak tonight, but no need to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: TONIGHT, UNDER, H (end of 'strength') and NO are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce or sparse, like few people standing on a field, an idiom for being scarce.

clue.text: Is inclined to ban wife from car

indicators.note: to ban the wife from the car is to remove her letter from it

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A husband tends towards forbidding his spouse to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is inclined' looks like a mood but means tilts over, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans to one side is said to heel, so it tilts or slants.

clue.text: Board finish — director off to pub with Leo

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of place, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film director heads off to the pub with a friend called Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like 'heading off' but signals a shuffle of TO, PUB and LEO. The board is a dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts, the twenty double ring is a classic way to finish a game on the dartboard.

clue.text: Reached high point of teaching: keeping student body away!

indicators.note: one word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: a creed is a set of teachings or beliefs

indicators.note: with the body, the middle, of student taken away, only its outer letters are left

explanation.surface: A school reaches the peak of its teaching but bans the student union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'student body' wants to be the union; here the body (middle) of 'student' goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: To crest a hill or wave is to reach its top, a summit.

clue.text: Get friendly with fellow's bird in lift

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow

indicators.note: one word sits in the other

parts.note: to lift is to raise
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone chats up a man's girlfriend in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for girlfriend, but here it is just a seabird; 'lift' (British for elevator) is the verb raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix socially and amicably with others, especially those on an opposing side.

clue.text: Lecture about producing waste

indicators.note: the words are producing the answer from within themselves

explanation.surface: A lecture that wanders around and produces nothing useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogen compound the body excretes in urine, so a waste product.

clue.text: /13. Is fairly shrewd at work (not showing up!)

indicators.note: up means in a mess, as in 'something is up', so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone clever at their job who is never seen there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not showing up' reads as being absent, but 'up' alone is the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means has a fair amount of experience and knowledge.

clue.text: Ex-pupil stole new drug — is no longer employed

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: new means the word stole is made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A former pupil stole a new drug and lost their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; 'no longer employed' means no longer used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date and no longer in use is outmoded.

clue.text: See 11
Illumination — one left blazing during darkness?

indicators.note: one piece occurs during the other, inside it

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

indicators.note: blazing means wild and fiery, so the word one is shaken up

explanation.surface: One lamp left burning through the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blazing' looks literal, a lamp alight, but it is the scramble signal; 'during' puts the pieces inside the darkness word.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing gas-filled tube used in signs is a form of lighting.

clue.text: Lush Roger now very drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the words are staggered about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Roger, a heavy drinker, is now very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like a drunkard (the noun) but is the adjective for thick vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxuriant vegetation that has grown thick and wild is rank, rampant growth.

clue.text: Match drawn saved season

indicators.note: saved means kept inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
D is the abbreviation for drawn in sports results tables

explanation.surface: A match drawn rescued a team's whole season.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British name for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tide is an old word for a time or season, kept in Yuletide and Eastertide.

clue.text: Put out? Nothing doing

indicators.note: out means not in place, so the letters of the word are disordered

parts.note: O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone feels put out, and does nothing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out?' looks like feeling offended.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'what are you up to?', the phrase means engaged in or busy with.

clue.text: Not all VIPs were relaxing in trailer

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the letters, rearranging them
not all of the word is used, as its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Some celebrities were lounging in a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' drops S from VIPS; VIP and WERE are then shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer for a film is an advance showing of clips.

clue.text: Force half-back on trial to play

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force, so the word gives THE

indicators.note: only half of the phrase is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: the second half of the Met, read back
a trial is an annoying person or thing, a pest

explanation.surface: A rugby half-back is forced to play on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-back' looks like a rugby position, but turns the second half of THE MET to give TEM; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late drama of Prospero's island is a stage work.

clue.text: Female accommodating passion put condom on?

indicators.note: accommodating means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
heat is passion

explanation.surface: A passionate woman puts a condom on her partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a jokey example of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something into a close-fitting case or cover, as a sword into a scabbard.

clue.text: Faint Welsh emblem?

parts.note: the leek is the emblem of Wales; the answer's first word turned over spells it

explanation.surface: An emblem of Wales, perhaps feeling a bit weak.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the word for a ship's spine, turned over, gives LEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse suddenly in a swoon or fall over is to pass out.

clue.text: Checks climbing plant

parts.note: to vet is to check
CH is an abbreviation for check, as in chess

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a plant climbing up a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' gives two checks, one word each.
explanation.definitionFit: A leguminous plant that climbs using tendrils, grown for fodder.

clue.text: Look increasingly imposing once resistance's quashed

indicators.note: quashed means suppressed, so a letter is removed

parts.note: grander means more imposing
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Appearing more impressive once opposition has been crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' is a noun here: a quick glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gander is British slang for having a quick glance.

clue.text: Dig uncovered bit of gold that's buried

indicators.note: buried means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: nude means uncovered, bare

indicators.note: just a bit, the first letter, of gold is taken

explanation.surface: A dig reveals a gold nugget that had been buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like an excavation but is a poke with the elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dig in the ribs is a prod or a poke.

clue.text: Island that is backing Germans

indicators.note: backing means turning back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
G stands for German, and GG for more than one

explanation.surface: An island that is supporting German people.
explanation.walkthrough: Eigg is a small island in Scotland's Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Hebridean isle off the west coast of Scotland, a place surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Out! Tory regularly found lying about combat service abroad

indicators.note: lying about means strewn around, so the letters are scattered
regularly means every other letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A Tory is caught out lying about military service overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT, TORY and FUD (alternate letters of 'found') are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A posting of fixed length overseas for soldiers is their spell on duty.

clue.text: Currently engaged? (No)

parts.note: the word no is the word on with its two letters switched

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is betrothed at the moment, answered no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' is a pun on electric current; read the answer as an instruction and ON switched gives the clue's 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: A device with electric current flowing through it is operating, powered up.

clue.text: Flat seventeen's occupant

indicators.note: the occupant lives inside, so the answer is found inside the word

explanation.surface: Who lives in flat number seventeen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A level or smooth surface has no bumps.
